status: researched requirements; not an implemented API contract

coverage.live: Available in the current sampled API and user interface for its documented population.
coverage.custom: Current numeric expression/point/filter collector can provide it when the graph authors the required value and semantics; no automatic lifecycle or event binding.
coverage.partial: A constrained implementation, manual derivation, or related evidence exists, but the generic requested capability is incomplete.
coverage.core: A mathematical core representation/reducer exists; this does not imply generic live collection or full UI support.
coverage.planned: Required or optional new capability; not implemented by this research.

priorities.P0: Core release evidence or immediately needed when the relevant mechanic exists.
priorities.P1: Required for applicable complex/stateful models or advanced verification.
priorities.P2: Specialized estimator or optional design/session analysis.

notation.N: Number of completed independent paid rounds, unless the family declares another subject.
notation.B: External wager charged for a paid round, including mode costs.
notation.W: Final settled payout of the complete paid round.
notation.X: W divided by fixed parent stake; a bonus buy may have a different external cost.
notation.A_f: Allocated additive payout component f per paid round, zero when absent.
notation.Y: A typed numeric value on the selected subject.
notation.F: A specified event or feature predicate.
notation.C: Proven final payout bound in the same units as the measured payout.
notation.p_pruned: Unresolved probability mass, not renormalized away.

families.name: Exposure, counts and accounting
families.subject: Explicit round, episode, reveal, award or node-visit population
metrics: Count completely settled paid rounds; denominator for fixed-stake round statistics
Count started rounds, including interrupted work; never substitute for completed exposure
Count rounds discarded before settlement and classify cancellation or runtime failure
Count visits or completed rounds considered by a metric before filter/value evaluation
Count subjects satisfying scope with a valid value
Count subjects for which the valid Boolean scope is false
Count missing/type/nonfinite/expression errors; critical measurements cannot pass by ignoring them
Count execution of a selected flattened point, including repeated loop visits
Count unique rounds or episodes containing at least one matching child event
Count explicit lifecycle entry events, distinguishing multiple instances in one round
Count matched lifecycle exits and reconcile open/interrupted episodes
Count typed base/FS/respin/cascade reveals, not all node visits
Count unique settled award IDs; detect duplicate crediting separately
Expected ledger total minus actual settlement; exact zero required under declared rounding

families.name: Wagers, return and payout components
families.subject: Completed paid round with externally charged wager and settled payout
metrics: sum B, including ante/buy/extra charges exactly once
mean X for independent complete rounds at the same external cost
sum W / sum B; not the unweighted mean of individual payout/wager ratios
Expected settled payout divided by cost from an independent model with stated assumptions
sum(W-B); house result has the opposite sign under this accounting model
1 - theoretical RTP for the defined mode and cost
E[A_f] across all paid rounds, including zeros for absent components
E[A_f] / E[X] when total expected payout is positive
E[Y | declared subject scope]; not automatically an RTP contribution
E[settled payout for mode] / externally charged mode cost
Total settled return minus allocated component returns and declared adjustments
Settled monetary amount under declared rounding minus exact pre-rounding amount

families.name: Event frequencies and probabilities
families.subject: One independent parent subject or explicitly dependent event population
metrics: P(X=0), complementary to round hit probability when observations are valid
P(0<X<1); distinguish from zero payout and actual player profit
P(W>B) for the subject's actual external cost
matching valid count / all eligible observations; with errors this is descriptive, not a clean event probability
P(at least one feature F in a paid round), counting each parent once
Number of F entries / eligible paid rounds; may exceed one
P(F | eligible subject predicate), with a declared denominator and no ignored invalid data
P(Y>=t), P(Y>t) or declared band membership with pinned inclusive/exclusive boundaries
1/p labeled one-in-k eligible subjects; undefined at zero estimated p, not a guaranteed gap

families.name: Numeric summary and higher moments
families.subject: Typed numeric value on the declared subject after any inner reduction
metrics: sum Y over matching valid subjects
min Y over matching valid subjects; undefined with zero matches
max Y over matching valid subjects; does not establish theoretical reachability limits
sum Y / matching valid subject count
E[Y^2] or its declared sample estimator
Population E[Y^2]-E[Y]^2, or sample M2/(n-1); label the convention
sqrt declared variance; sample SD undefined below two valid observations
sigma/mean under a declared valid positive-mean convention
Third standardized central moment with explicit sample/bias convention and undefined cases
Fourth standardized central moment; declare raw versus excess and sample correction
E[abs(Y-center)] for an explicitly fixed or estimated center

families.name: Discrete support, histograms, CDF and tails
families.subject: One declared numeric population; fixed stake or explicit normalization
metrics: Count or exact rational probability of each distinct value in a bounded support
Number of Y values in pinned semantic bins
sum Y within each bin; cannot reconstruct this from bin counts alone
sum of round payouts in band / total turnover, or fixed-stake E[X 1{band}]
F(t)=P(Y<=t); histogram-only evidence is exact for observed counts at bin boundaries
P(Y>=t) with explicit discrete boundary convention
Q(q)=inf{x:F(x)>=q}; distinguish exact support, histogram bounds and sketch estimates
E[Y 1{Y>=t}] with the full eligible population denominator
E[Y 1{Y>=t}]/P(Y>=t), undefined if the denominator is zero
Mean of exactly the upper 1-q probability mass, splitting ties at Q(q)
Share of total payout from a declared top fraction of subjects with a tie rule

families.name: Feature lifecycle, inner reductions and FS accounting
families.subject: One typed feature episode, with parent paid-round identity
metrics: Probability of each selected type among eligible feature entries, and unconditional activation separately
Sum allocated awards within each episode, then measure across episodes
One value per matching FS/respin/cascade reveal, not one value per episode
FS/respin budget recorded once at episode entry
Sum newly awarded FS/respins during the episode, not repeated remaining-counter reads
Count typed reveals within the episode and report duration distribution
initial+additional-played-removed; equals recorded remaining at every boundary
Reveals explicitly forfeited by authored termination rules
Count retrigger events with opportunities and type-specific award rules
P(at least one retrigger | eligible episode), using episode Boolean any reduction
Value distribution by FS/respin/cascade index with parent-episode identity
Ordinary completion, payout cap, authored stop, budget, cancellation and error separately

families.name: Symbol, award and rule-specific diagnostics
families.subject: Mapped draw, visible board, evaluated reveal or unique award as specified
metrics: Observed or exact frequency of each stop against authored strip weights
Symbol counts by reel/position/reveal type; do not assume uniform visible symbols
Winning symbol, substituted symbol, leading/all Wild case and length per line
Number of payable line awards in a reveal under overlapping-award rules
Product of matching position counts for each payable combination
Count scatters with reel/location eligibility and pay/trigger rule mapping
Connected component sizes and awarded components under authored adjacency
Wild membership, substitution and ownership follow the chosen rule, including shared clusters
New/retained/removed cells and occupancy before/after a reveal; reset at correct episode boundary
Depth distribution, payout by depth, removal/survivor/refill correctness
Unique collected values, respin resets, terminal occupancy and exactly-once award settlement
Multiplier states, transitions and awards after the authored application order
Return from distinct symbol/line/scatter/cluster award classes with overlap policy
Outcome distribution and EV for each allowed policy in a choice-sensitive game

families.name: State processes, reachability and termination
families.subject: Explicit ordered state transitions, feature episode or persistent regeneration cycle
metrics: Count typed before/after state pairs in the intended subject order
Count(i->j)/eligible departures from i, compared with authored transition law
Time/step-weighted occupancy under a declared initial/reset/persistent regime
Consecutive steps spent in each state, including boundary censoring
Probability of each absorbing result, including distinct game and resource stops
For a valid finite transient Q, (I-Q)^-1 times the vector of ones
Expected transient visits multiplied by correctly defined per-state/transition rewards
Mean new reveals generated per eligible reveal in a specified branching model
Reachability and probability of never reaching the authored terminal state
Long-run payout/turnover using a justified recurrent-state or regenerative analysis
Count transitions violating authored episode and paid-round reset/persistence policies

families.name: Paired values, covariance and ordered sequences
families.subject: Paired values on the same parent subject or ordered logical subject stream
metrics: Cov(A_f,A_g) from paired per-round values including absent-component zeros
Cov(Y,Z)/(sd(Y)*sd(Z)); undefined when either SD is zero
Var(sum A_f)-sum Var(A_f)-2 sum pair covariance; expected residual zero
Ordered subject correlation at configured lags under a declared dependence null
Completed inter-event gaps plus explicitly censored leading/trailing exposure
Lengths of consecutive predicate successes/failures in logical order
Subject-level output difference under a defined random coupling, with paired uncertainty

families.name: Generating distributions and independence diagnostics
families.subject: Named mapped RNG draws under the declared game model
metrics: Draw outcome counts compared with exact WeightSet probabilities
Difference between intended probabilities and the distribution induced by scaling/shuffling
Serial correlation/runs diagnostics under intended independence or authored state conditioning
Joint outcomes versus intended joint law, preserving without-replacement dependencies
Stream duplication diagnostics versus the probability of legitimate repeated outcomes
Compare draw frequencies to each explicitly authored state-dependent distribution

families.name: Cap, pruning, truncation and rare-event guarantees
families.subject: Raw and settled payout paired per round; retained exact mass or weighted rare-event sample
metrics: P(settled payout=C), including exact equality; not the clipping counter
P(raw payout>C) before settlement and under the declared stop policy
E[raw payout-settled payout] with valid paired raw/settled accounting
Maximum supported by the complete authored model, distinguished from sample maximum and declared cap
Missing exact mass retained without renormalizing survivors
known first moment <= E[X] <= known first moment+p_pruned*C when the finite bound is valid
known event mass <= P(F) <= min(1,known event mass+p_pruned)
Bound unresolved second moment by p_pruned*C^2, then use compatible mean/second-moment constraints
Probability and reward impact of budget stops, separately from authored terminal rules
1-alpha^(1/n) for independent fixed-count Bernoulli subjects with no successes
Proposal coverage, weight sums/extremes and effective-size diagnostic; not a stand-alone guarantee
Correctly likelihood-weighted event/return estimator with a justified variance and support contract

families.name: Independent references, equivalence and distribution tests
families.subject: Compatible model/reference populations with explicit precision and error budget
metrics: Observed-minus-independent-reference mean, with units and uncertainty
Observed event probability minus compatible reference probability
Per-round component return versus independent feature reference
Rational equality of outcome probability maps on independent small reference models
sup_t abs(F_observed(t)-F_reference(t)); test calibration must match discrete/tied data
Pearson or exact/calibrated multinomial test with pinned bins and validated sparse-count treatment
Appropriate interval contained in the authored reference tolerance band; compatibility alone is weaker
Count exact failures and retain bounded replayable witnesses
Change in return/events/tails under an explicit parameter perturbation with independent or defined paired inference

families.name: Sampling precision, error control and sufficiency
families.subject: Independent subjects, clusters or a justified dependent-process estimator
metrics: Independent rounds/episodes/cycles used by inference; not the number of correlated child visits
s/sqrt(n) only when the subject/variance assumptions are appropriate
Declared fixed-count approximate or valid bounded/dependent estimator interval
Validated Wilson/exact or appropriate dependent-subject interval including zero/all events
Paired payout/wager inference for the ratio of sums; not a constant-stake mean interval
Inference using independent parent rounds/episodes or a validated cluster estimator
Declared approximation/bound based on variance, event rarity, tolerance and error level
Predeclared simultaneous testing/error control across required measurements
Confidence sequence or validated repeated-look design for automated acceptance/stopping
Precision, expected event count, invalid data, unresolved mass and inference assumptions meet the acceptance profile

families.name: Evidence identity and execution consistency
families.subject: Pinned graph, measurement definition, run and calculation mode
metrics: Same inputs/stream reproduce payouts and aggregates; this establishes reproducibility, not mathematical correctness
Final outcomes and aggregates invariant under supported worker counts with fixed logical chunks
Production execution versus independent/reference semantics on the same authored models
UI save/load/API AST produces the same validated graph and behavior
Recovered durable prefix, counters and measurement plan agree without fabricating lost work
Bounded subject-level state/event evidence and replay coordinates for an assertion failure

families.name: Optional session and game-experience analysis
families.subject: Declared ordered session with bankroll, wager and stopping rules
metrics: Distribution of sum(W-B) over a declared finite session; include state and cost rules
P(session net result>0) for declared horizon and stopping policy
Probability of no event over a declared horizon; do not assume geometric gaps in stateful models
Largest ordered bankroll decline from a previous session peak
Probability of inability to fund the next allowed wager before the horizon
Distribution of rounds until a defined stop/exhaustion/target condition
First-passage distribution to a defined feature under actual state/reset rules
Distribution of the maximum settled round payout within a declared session

constraints: Families and parameterized instances are a researched catalogue, not a universal certification checklist.
All probabilities require compatible numerator, denominator, subject and invalid-data policies.
Feature components require attribution and settlement rules; overlapping cohorts do not add to total return.
Custom values require explicit units and proven bounds before any finite guarantee is applied.
RTP compatibility, reproducibility and absence of observed defects are distinct from a proof of the complete mathematical model.
Session measurements are optional design analysis; persistent mechanics and RNG security require additional applicable review.
